rationale: A wins because it interrogates the strongest supplied fact instead of decorating it: "Substack says its top creators split more than $400M last year — and won't say how the split works" is a real reporter assignment with denominator, gross/net, fees, refunds, and audit questions built in. B has usable bones, but "Substack completes its swap from email newsletter to all-in-video media app" overstates the facts and "The numbers behind Substack's 'struggling platform' reputation don't add up" tries to make a contrarian finance story before it has the evidence. A is sharper, better bounded, and much less likely to send a founder into a reporter's inbox with a half-built premise.
gaps_in_A: "Substack has stopped competing with Mailchimp and started competing with YouTube" is punchy but a little too categorical; the update supports a move toward video/media-app competition, not that it has stopped competing in newsletters/email altogether.

"Video hosting is one of the most expensive infrastructure commitments a platform can make" is plausible but not supplied in the update; A correctly asks for proof, but the line itself edges toward unsourced cost-structure assertion.

The funding angle depends on "public funding struggles" but A only has the generic fact block; it admits this is unpitchable without sourcing, which is good, but the angle remains the weakest kept one.
A could have made the podcast-specific implication cleaner instead of folding it mostly into writer/video labor and category strategy.
gaps_in_B: "completes its swap from email newsletter to all-in-video media app" is overclaiming. Native video plus a feed does not prove a completed swap or an all-video strategy.
"short-form, algorithmic-style feed" invents mechanics not in the update. The facts say TikTok-style feed; they do not say short-form or algorithmic ranking.

"The numbers behind Substack's 'struggling platform' reputation don't add up" is a contrarian claim the supplied facts cannot carry. B admits it needs prior reporting and denominator proof, but the headline already sells the conclusion.

The first two angles are padded cousins: "media app" and "in the ring with YouTube and TikTok" are not cleanly distinct enough because both use the same feed/video repositioning evidence with nearly the same protagonist.
